emailSequence.subject: Your AI compliance gameplan
emailSequence.preview: A practical next-step map for AI governance and legal readiness.
emailSequence.body: Your scorecard is a starting point, not a legal conclusion. The useful next step is to turn the risk areas into an inventory, owner map, vendor review, and 30/60/90-day implementation plan.

emailSequence.subject: Vendor risk is often the first AI legal risk
emailSequence.preview: AI legal readiness often starts with the contract stack.
emailSequence.body: Before a policy solves anything, a company needs to know which AI vendors touch data, what rights the vendor has, and where confidentiality, IP ownership, indemnity, audit, and security terms live.

emailSequence.subject: Colorado AI readiness without overreacting
emailSequence.preview: How to treat unsettled law as a readiness workstream.
emailSequence.body: Colorado AI and ADMT rules are moving. That does not mean companies should freeze. It means readiness should focus on use-case inventory, consequential decision exposure, human review, notices, records, and governance ownership.

emailSequence.subject: Turn AI use into a legal operating system
emailSequence.preview: The goal is repeatable governance, not one-off panic.
emailSequence.body: A durable AI legal system includes intake, approval, vendor review, documentation, escalation, training, and board-ready reporting. That is the workstream behind an AI Compliance Readiness Sprint.
